awd_titl_txt: Travel: NSF Student Travel Grant for the 2025 ACM SIGSPATIAL International Conference on Advances in Geographic Information Systems (ACM SIGSPATIAL)
awd_abstract_narration:
This activity is for proposed travel awards for 25 U.S.-based graduate and undergraduate students to participate in the 33rd ACM SIGSPATIAL GIS 2025 Conference, which will be held in Minneapolis, Minnesota, November 3-6, 2025. The Conference is annually organized by the ACM (Association for Computing Machinery) Special Interest Group on Spatial Information (SIGSPATIAL), which is an association for researchers, students, and professionals interested in research, development, and deployment of solutions to spatial information handling and spatial knowledge extraction problems. The Conference started in 1993, has established itself as the world's premier research conference in spatial computing, spatial data, and geographic information systems (GIS); it provides a forum for original research contributions covering all conceptual, design, and implementation aspects of GIS ranging from applications, user interfaces, and visualization to storage management and indexing issues. Besides the technical program, the conference features workshops, a student research competition, a PhD workshop, a data competition, demos, and networking events. The importance of spatial information handling continuously increases with new application domains and the availability and ubiquity of large spatial data such as maps, remote-sensing images, 3D medical atlases, and the decennial census. Businesses, industry, academia, and governmental agencies utilize spatial information to improve their daily operations, structure new strategies, and increase overall productivity and US competitiveness.

Spatial data and applications pose novel research challenges in a wide variety of sub-areas, including (but not limited to) spatial information acquisition, modeling, data structures, algorithms, analysis, querying \& integration, human-computer interaction \& visualization, and systems \& architectures. From these sub-areas, deep research questions emerge that are motivated by a broad range of applications (e.g., emergency and crisis management, environmental monitoring, global positioning and location detection, geosciences, location-based and mobile services, navigation, and route planning). ACM SIGPATIAL has provided a forum for this research, including presentations of accepted technical papers, poster and demo exhibition encouraging lively interaction among all participants, and presentations by leading related industry members. The participation of U.S. graduate and aspiring undergraduate students will result in the intellectual stimulation of young minds to pursue advanced research and development activities in an area that has a huge technical and societal impact

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.

por.por_cntn:
NSF funding supported the participation of twenty-five students at the 33rd ACM SIGSPATIAL International Conference on Advances in Geographic Information Systems (ACM SIGSPATIAL 2025) in Minneapolis, MN, USA. These students represented eighteen U.S. universities across twelve states, comprising a cohort of three undergraduate student, one master's student, and twenty-one Ph.D. students. The four-day conference is the flagship international forum for research on spatial data science, geospatial artificial intelligence, urban computing, mobility modeling, and spatial data management, bringing together leading experts from academia, industry, and government

Every funded student actively shaped the conference dialogue by showcasing their cutting-edge research across multiple scholarly channels. Students delivered oral research presentations, participated in topical workshops, presented live system demonstrations, and competed in the prestigious Student Research Competition. These platforms rocketed their visibility within the spatial computing community, yielding invaluable expert feedback and accelerating their professional growth. 

 

Beyond spotlighting research, the conference prioritized building a supportive community. A dedicated lunchtime mentoring event matched students with senior researchers, sparking rich conversations in an informal, welcoming setting. The profound impact of this experience shines through the students' own words:

Ruichen W. reflected: "I was able to share my work through my presentation and in-depth conversations during the poster session, and I even formed some potential future collaborations.",

Min M. shared: "[...] I also met other professors and scholars who are interested in my project, and I am now brainstorming and working with them on how to conduct the research together. SIGSPATIAL genuinely has given me many opportunities to connect with people and has expanded my research career path.",

and Nicole S. reported: "By attending this workshop I made connections with a faculty member that is now considering me for a postdoc position if one arises in their lab."

These testimonial highlights the enduring scholarly value of the program and underscores the essential role of NSF support in facilitating student participation at high-impact venues. By removing financial barriers, this initiative empowered the next generation of researchers to engage deeply with the spatial computing community, contribute innovative ideas, and cultivate collaborations that will extend well beyond the conference itself.
